rv.q: Actually, this inventive new version of Pedro Almodovar’s 1988 classic film is a stylish hoot – a fiesta of PMT with monstrous, ticklish caricatures and, ultimately, a heart very much in the right place.
But this becomes a joyous evening: an affectionate, poignant and defiant tribute to female resilience.
Thanks to a fizzier and more fluent second half this is a musical that leaves one feeling well entertained.
It all makes for a perfectly pleasant show in which only the songs, in adding depth to character, put a brake on the story's propulsion.
“Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown” may have a clunky title – that is a nightmare to keep typing – but is a fantastic show from start to finish.

cn.t: This energetic musical adaptation of Almodóvar's film delivers giddy farce and camp theatricality, led by Tamsin Greig's sparky performance. Critics find it screwball fun with smart songwriting, though some note structural issues and occasional naffness.
